evidence.text:
Indoctrination was the term for the brainwashing effect the Reapers and their technology exerted on organic beings. A signal or energy field around a Reaper subtly influenced the minds of nearby organics; it was first reported to Shepard by Eden Prime farmers who described a "horrible noise" from Sovereign, and Matriarch Benezia noted that even Sovereign's confusing interior angles served indoctrination. The effect extended to Reaper artifacts, such as the one aboard the MSV Cornucopia that brainwashed its crew. The salarian lieutenant Ganto Imness called it a greater threat than a krogan army. As Vigil explained, the Reapers used indoctrinated slaves from conquered worlds as sleeper agents against the Protheans, then abandoned them to die when they withdrew.

The mechanics were poorly understood but believed to involve an electromagnetic field and infrasound/ultrasound stimulating the brain and limbic system, producing headaches, hallucinations, paranoia, or superstitious awe, and ultimately letting the Reaper use the victim's body to amplify its signal as voices in the mind. Rana Thanoptis, an asari neuroscientist on Virmire, described it as a subtle whisper that compels action without reason; over roughly a week of exposure the subject stops thinking and merely obeys, becoming a mindless husk-like servant, the fate of her predecessor and Kirrahe's captured men. Saren Arterius discovered a balance between control and usefulness: the more control Sovereign had, the less capable the subject, so Saren made himself an invaluable resource to find the Conduit and win a reprieve.

Mental damage was severe and permanent. Only those with immense mental strength could resist, and only briefly. Benezia kept a "haven" in her mind but was trapped watching herself commit atrocities, choosing death on Noveria: "I am not myself, I never will be again." The last Rachni Queen was immune or highly resistant, forcing the Reapers to physically restrain her while she bred warriors. The asari Shiala was the only sentient being to fully escape, because the Thorian's control supplanted Sovereign's. Ironically, indoctrination contributed to Sovereign's defeat: after Virmire, Saren's faltering resolve required cybernetic implants to reinforce control, and when Saren died the Reaper's diverted energy to animate his corpse left Sovereign's shields down and vulnerable to the Alliance Navy, a flaw other Reapers such as Harbinger did not display.

The page also covers similar phenomena: Thorian enthrallment (pain-based conditioning, resistible by disciplined minds, granting cohesion among thralls, ending at the Thorian's death); geth programming (the Reaper virus given to the heretics, and the 2186 geth submitting to a broadcast Reaper code on Rannoch, amplified through a shackled Legion/Geth VI aboard a geth dreadnought); Cerberus experiments (Reaper-grade neural implants used in "integration" at the Barn and Project Phoenix, and Henry Lawson replicating the Reaper signal at Sanctuary on Horizon under the Illusive Man, who was later implanted with Reaper nanotech aboard Cronos Station and briefly controlled Shepard and David Anderson on the Citadel); and Leviathan enthrallment via opalescent artifacts, which caused no long-term mental damage aside from memory loss and was the basis for Reaper indoctrination.

evidence.text:
Admiral Daro'Xen vas Moreh was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board known for her clinical intellect and keen scientific interest in the geth, whom she regarded as machines built solely to serve their creators. She was said to have performed surgery on her childhood toys without guilt. She wished to return the geth to quarian control.

In Mass Effect 2, Xen was one of three admirals judging Tali'Zorah's treason trial, alongside Zaal'Koris vas Qwib Qwib and Han'Gerrel vas Neema. She viewed the trial as "a farce born of fear," called Zaal'Koris a coward and Han'Gerrel "an aging warship," and considered war with the geth foolish, though she had no qualms about experimenting on active geth. If Shepard brought Legion, she found it fascinating and mused about experimenting on it, prompting Legion to state it was not available and to call her control plans "unsound," a view Tali shared. Afterward she messaged Shepard that had Rael'Zorah's research been presented, humanity would have benefited; instead the quarians would reclaim their homeworld and the largest synthetic army in the galaxy.

In Mass Effect 3, Xen's research and development corps created white-noise jamming against geth ladar systems, prompting the Admiralty to vote for war, and she led the Special Projects group. If Tali was absent, Xen provided electronic support during the mission to disable a geth dreadnought, gave Shepard a prototype Arc Pistol, and later left in a geth fighter. She created the Sync Laser marking technology that cut through geth jamming, critical to the assault on the Reaper base on Rannoch. She repeatedly expressed interest in dissecting Legion or the Geth VI, argued with Tali over search-and-rescue versus salvage priorities, and briefed Shepard on the rescue of Admiral Koris. If she survived the geth-quarian war, she was sent to help build the Crucible, where Shala'Raan vas Tonbay described her as dissatisfied with the device but lending her technical skills. She was voiced by Claudia Black.

evidence.text: At the climax Shepard must choose between peace, or geth genocide, or quarian genocide: give the geth full sentience (the Reaper upgrade) at the cost of the quarian fleet, or destroy the geth to save the quarians. - **Shepard sides with the quarians:** Tali kills Legion (or shuts the geth down) with a "flat shovel blade." She has done what quarian society expects, but — because of her history with Legion — she expresses regret, and answers Legion's last question, "Does this unit have a soul?", with a solemn "Yes… yes, it does." Legion, in his last moments, ignores Shepard and turns all his attention to Tali, the comrade who stabbed him — "a mirror image of himself." - **Shepard sides with the geth:** Tali begs Shepard not to choose the geth over her people. If Shepard uploads the code, Tali — as Admiral Tali'Zorah — calls off the quarian fleet's attack over the comm, and Legion sacrifices himself to disseminate the code ("copy code is insufficient; direct personality dissemination required"). - **Botched path (Shepard failed to broker peace and the war is one-sided):** Tali is powerless to stop Han'Gerrel, Rael, and Daro'Xen, whose hubris blinds them; as what remains of the quarian fleet burns in Rannoch's atmosphere — Captain Ysra of the Rayya over the radio — Tali, having done everything she could, takes her own life before her home ship burns. The essayist frames this as the completion of her arc: her instilled sense of duty is useless when there is no Fleet to serve, and her unrequited love for family can no longer hope for a brighter future.

evidence.text: Against Koris's objections, and Tali's if she is appointed as an admiral, the other admirals chose to attack the geth, which caused them to seek help from the Reapers. evidence.text:
Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib-Qwib was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board, outspoken in his sympathy for the geth. He firmly opposed reclaiming the quarian homeworld, arguing that the sentient geth had as much right to live as the quarians and that the Migrant Fleet should colonize a new world instead. This earned him the label of geth apologist; Han'Gerrel vas Neema called him a "whining suit-wetter" and Daro'Xen vas Moreh considered him a coward. He was initially distrustful of Rael'Zorah and his daughter Tali, though he later admitted he never hated Tali and only opposed her father's aim of war against the geth. His home vessel, the Qwib-Qwib, was a formerly owned ship whose embarrassing registry name he refused to change over "petty insults."

During Tali'Zorah's treason hearing in Mass Effect 2, Koris objected to Commander Shepard defending her, saying a human had no business in sensitive quarian military matters; Shala'Raan overruled him because Tali had been declared crew of the Normandy SR-2. If Shepard brought Legion, Koris instead demanded the geth be removed from the courtroom and accused Tali of intimidation, but withdrew when reminded the Rayya's captain had permitted Legion aboard. Koris was quick to conclude Shepard and Tali had died retaking the Alarei and moved to have Tali posthumously exiled, prompting objections from Raan and Gerrel before the pair returned alive.

In Mass Effect 3, the other admirals attacked the geth over Koris's objections, driving the geth to the Reapers; Koris feared this had doomed the quarian race and took command of the Civilian Fleet. His ship was shot down while destroying a geth planetary cannon; he survived the crash but was cut off from his crew. Shepard could obey his plea to save his crew instead of him, or convince him to return. If rescued, Koris talked panicking captains into staying, contributed to the war effort, and backed Shepard in brokering quarian-geth peace, lending his authority when Shepard ordered all quarian ships to cease fire. If left, he died charging a Geth Prime with a primed grenade, and some Civilian Fleet captains fled and were cut down, reducing quarian combat effectiveness.

evidence.text: Admiral Xen's corps of research and development eventually create a means to cause massive white\-noise jamming against the highly precise geth ladar scanning systems, giving the quarian fleet a major advantage in any attempt to wage war against the geth. Upon this revelation, the Admiralty votes to go to war, with Admiral Koris and possibly Tali dissenting (if she was exonerated in her trial and subsequently promoted to her father's vacant Admiral office). Xen leads the Special Projects group during the war. If Tali is absent, Xen provides assistance to Shepard during their mission to disable a geth dreadnought. Unlike Tali, she doesn't fight through the ship, instead advancing to the operations center when Shepard has cleared the way and providing electronic support, later leaving with them in a geth fighter. Xen takes pride in her technological contributions that initially drove the geth back, preferring the present war over Raan's bloodless caution or Koris's geth sympathies, although Reaper involvement turned the tables on her race. Nevertheless, she continues to create anti\-synthetic countermeasures like the Arc Pistol and personally gives a prototype to Shepard aboard the dreadnought if Tali isn't around. Shepard's squadmates have differing opinions on the weapon, although Xen gives her own in two cases. If EDI points out the illegality of polonium rounds against organics (which is roughly analogous to the Arc Pistol's effects against synthetics), Xen quips it's "fortunate" the prohibition doesn't apply against synthetics. If Liara comments that she knows people willing to pay handsomely for the weapon's design, Xen replies she's open for offers. After the mission's completion, Admiral Xen expresses interest in dissecting Legion (or the Geth VI if Legion is unavailable). Shepard can emphatically discourage against it and cut off Xen before she voices her views on potential scientific benefits. In the middle of the operation to reclaim Rannoch, Xen gets into an argument over inter\-ship comms with Tali over ship operations. Tali wants Xen's ships to do search and rescue ops for escape pods, while Xen wants to continue salvage operations on the destroyed Geth dreadnought, asserting the need to understand geth technology. Admiral Xen later briefs Shepard on the rescue mission for Admiral Koris, noting that the Civilian Fleet is in danger of breaking up without their leader. If the geth fighter squadrons attacking the liveships have been dealt with, Xen offers her expertise in dealing with other geth servers. Shepard suggests asking Legion/Geth VI but Xen claims the geth only says, "No data available" whenever she inquires. She then asks how the server's platoon of Geth Primes cooperated with the Commander. Upon hearing they volunteered, Xen reminds Shepard that she could "examine" these geth to confirm their allegiance. Admiral Xen creates a laser marking technology that can cut through the geth jamming signals, which essentially is the Sync Laser. This technology proves critical to Shepard's team during the assault on the Reaper base on Rannoch. Should Xen survive the resolution of the geth/quarian war, she will be sent to the Crucible to help with development and construction. She is described as being dissatisfied with the device by Admiral Shala'Raan vas Tonbay and uses her brilliant scientific and technical skills to assist with the construction. Also, if Shepard supported Xen over Tali during their argument regarding escape pods, Xen is able to salvage useful materials for the war effort.

evidence.text: Once the now\-sentient geth realized what the quarians were doing, they retaliated. Initially only some geth began to take up arms in order to protect other units that could not defend themselves. The quarians placed their worlds under martial law, hunting down even those geth not participating in the hostilities, which was opposed by a large portion of the quarian people. They sheltered geth from the authorities, and were detained or killed as a result. Eventually, the opposition became an outnumbered minority unable to prevent the outbreak of all\-out war in 1895 CE. The geth emerged victorious within a year, overrunning the quarians' colonies and their homeworld of Rannoch. During the war, they committed a brutal genocide that eradicated all but a few million of the quarians\- less than one percent of the pre\-war population. The surviving quarians fled aboard their starships. Having lost their homes, the quarians pleaded for help from the Citadel Council, but were denied aid and stripped of their embassy as punishment for violating the Council's laws against creating artificial intelligences. All told, the Geth War resulted in the loss of billions of quarian lives, and inflicted irreparable damage to their economy and culture.
